result:
result: Rune is not a TUI. It is a GPU-rendered native Rust GUI framework (wgpu + winit). A faithful "terminal dashboard in rune" does not exist, so the root should decide whether to port to a GUI window. The notes file was not written because this role has no Write tool. The condensed cheat sheet is inline below.

**What it is (sourced)**
- The README says "A native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, with its own renderer, text, layout and springs" (https://github.com/anomalyco/rune).
- AGENTS.md says "A Rust GPU UI framework (wgpu, winit)". It lists Mac, Windows, Linux, web and iOS (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/rune/dev/AGENTS.md).
- License is MIT, default branch `dev`, created 2026-10-22. Edition 2024 workspace (`Cargo.toml`).
- There are no releases and no crates.io package. The README says: `rune = { git = "https://github.com/anomalyco/rune", rev = "<dev rev>" }`. It is pre-release and you pin a `dev` rev. `dev` is fast-forward only (AGENTS.md).
- Newest commit I saw is 757bcb1 (2026-11-09). That is a snapshot from the commits page, so re-check it before pinning.
- No pull requests are accepted (README).
- Anomaly's `hex` repo (https://github.com/anomalyco/hex/blob/dev/docs/plans/rune-ui.md) uses Rune on Windows. It describes a Windows tray app with a layered HUD. It is one early consumer.

**API cheat sheet (all from `crates/rune/README.md` and `examples/hello`, `examples/live-values`)**
- Entry point:
  ```rust
  fn view(s:&State,_:&mut Cx)->El { col().w_full().h_full().gap(16.0).fill(t.bg).child(text("x")) }
  fn main(){ rune::run(AppSpec::new("Title",(w,h),State::default,view)); }
  ```
  - Imports: `use rune::{AppSpec,Cx,El,col,row,el,text}; use rune::tok::{self,type_}`.
  - Theme: `tok::theme(true)`.
- State and reactivity:
  - Handlers are `.on_press(|s:&mut State| ..)`, plus `_tx` variants and `.on_drag`.
  - Handlers are queued, run between frames, then `view` re-runs and the diff retargets properties.
  - Give elements `.key("..")`. Hover and press never re-run `view`.
- Timers and refresh:
  - `AppSpec::setup(state, wake)` runs once and hands you a `Waker` for background threads.
  - `poll(state, clock, tx) -> bool` runs before each frame. Return true only when visible state changed.
  - `tx.wake_after(Duration)` schedules a poll.
  - `AppHandle::update(|s,tx| ..)` is `Send+Sync` and changes state from any thread. Every handle call wakes the loop.
  - Build the app with `App::new(spec).init(..)`, then `app.handle()`, then `app.run()`.
- Keyboard:
  - Window-level `AppSpec::on_key`, and per-element `on_key` and `.on_key_up`.
  - `.focusable(true)`, `.tab_index`, `.focus_group()` for arrow-key roving, `.focus_ring`.
  - Enter and Space activate controls.
  - Key routing order is documented in the README.
- Mouse:
  - Hit-testing, hover, `.on_press`, `.on_double_press`, `.on_secondary_press`, `.on_drag`, `.on_wheel`.
  - `.pointer_buttons([PointerButton::Middle])`.
  - `.cursor(..)`.
- Scrolling:
  - `.scroll(ScrollSpec{stick_bottom})`, `.scroll_x()`, `.scroll_xy()`.
  - Virtual rows: `.virtualize(est_row_h)` on a growth stack (`.growth(GrowthSpec)`) that is the first child of the scroll viewport.
  - `tx.scroll_into_view(key)`, `scroll_page`, `scroll_to`.
  - Gotchas: bound the ancestor height with `.h_full()` or `.min_h(0.0)` on each intermediate column, or the viewport collapses to 0.
- Tabs and lists:
  - `rune-kit` provides `SegmentedControl`, `TabStrip`, `Sidebar` with `virtual_rows`, `Toolbar`, `shell`, `SplitView`, `Progress`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Select` and `TextInput`. See https://github.com/anomalyco/rune/blob/dev/crates/rune-kit/README.md.
  - Arrow-key roving: roles `list`, `listbox`, `tree` use Up/Down; tabs and segments use Left/Right too.
- Drawing: `canvas(shape)` and `Shape` for polylines and fills. These suit sparklines and gauges.
- Testing, with no window or GPU:
  - `Runtime::new(state, view, (w,h), Env{system_dark:true,scale:2.0})`, then `rt.frame(dt)`, `rt.find(key)`, `rt.pointer_down/up`, `rt.presented(key)` (`examples/hello` test).
  - Headless flags: `-- --snap out.png --scene name`, `--tree`.

**Windows and native code (sourced plus inference)**
- Sourced: Windows is a supported target. The README documents the Windows DirectWrite text default and Windows input details (AltGr, Shift+wheel).
- Sourced: the workspace sets `unsafe_code = "allow"` for "GPU and FFI code". Apps are plain Rust, so `windows-sys` and IOCTL calls compile in the same crate. Rune has no FFI layer and needs none.
- Sourced: hex reports Windows was cross-compiled with `cargo xwin clippy ... --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and aarch64. Its first real Windows launch was still on a pending checklist, so Windows is less proven than Linux and macOS.
- Sourced: `run` panics when no display exists (CI). `App::try_run` returns an error instead.
- Inference: keep the Rust SMART/IOCTL backend unchanged as a library module or crate. Add a `rune` front end in place of the TUI view layer.
  - Run the collector on a `std::thread` and push snapshots with `AppHandle::update`, or use `poll` with `tx.wake_after`. This avoids blocking the UI thread.
  - Keep the `serde_json` history as is.
  - Model tabs as a `SegmentedControl` or `TabStrip`, drives and attributes as `virtualize`d rows, and key bindings in `on_key`.
- Inference: Linux CI can run `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test` (AGENTS.md commands). Test with `Runtime` headless (no display needed). Linux builds of Windows binaries are plausible via `cargo xwin`, per hex's note. I did not verify this for a standalone project.

**Caveats**
- Pre-release with frequent output-affecting changes (see CHANGELOG.md). The pinned rev is a risk.
- The result is a windowed GPU app, not a terminal one. It also adds a heavy dependency tree (wgpu, winit, Taffy, Parley), so it will not be "simple" in dependency terms.
- The `Cargo.toml` from the repo's own `chkdsk` was not read, because this role cannot read project files. The Assignment gave no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md rules for chkdsk. Please confirm whether the user really wants a GUI, since "terminal dashboard" implies a TUI.

questions: Should the app become a Rune GUI window, or stay a TUI (ratatui or similar)? Rune cannot render to a terminal.
